artworks.title: Pan and Syrinx
artworks.description: Boucher's National Gallery canvas: Pan reaches as Syrinx dissolves into reeds at the Ladon — Rococo flesh for Ovid's Arcadian escape.

artworks.title: Pan and Syrinx
artworks.description: De Troy stages the chase at the riverbank — Syrinx already turning toward the reeds while Pan's desire closes in. French Regency myth as soft pastoral crisis.

artworks.title: Pan and Syrinx
artworks.description: Hoet's Google Art Project panel: Pan and the nymph among trees and water — Dutch golden-age quiet before the reeds become the syrinx.

artworks.title: Pan and Syrinx
artworks.description: Dorigny's Baroque pursuit: goat-legged Pan and fleeing Syrinx — the moment before metamorphosis, painted as French classical chase.

artworks.title: The Nymph Syrinx
artworks.description: Liberi's Venetian Syrinx alone — the Arcadian nymph before Pan's pursuit, flesh and landscape waiting for Ovid's reed transformation.

music.title: Syrinx
music.description: Debussy's solo flute piece — originally for a theatrical Pan — keeps Syrinx's name as the sound of reeds turning into music.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book I — Syrinx flees Pan to the Ladon, becomes reeds, and lends her name to the pipes Pan cuts from her body.

popCulture.title: Syrinx
popCulture.description: The Arcadian nymph who became Pan's pipes — still the word for the reed instrument and for flight into song.
